description_short: The sword that slew Yamata no Orochi; one of the Three Sacred Treasures of Japan.
description_long: Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi (also called Ame-no-Murakumo-no-Tsurugi) is the sword that, in the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki, Susanoo drew from the tail of the eight-headed serpent Yamata no Orochi and offered to Amaterasu. [S1][S2] It is one of the Three Sacred Treasures (the Regalia) and the emblem of the imperial line's descent from the sun-goddess. In legend it quenched a great fire at Ise. [S2] As one of the Regalia it is the emblem of the emperor's divine right.
interesting_facts: Kusanagi is one of the Three Sacred Treasures (the Regalia) alongside the Yata no Kagami and the Yasakani no Magatama.
uncertainty_notes: The regalia are not publicly displayed or examined; the physical sword's survival and form are a matter of tradition, not of public verification.

description_short: The mirror that revealed the light; one of the Three Sacred Treasures of Japan.
description_long: Yata no Kagami ('the Eight-Span Mirror') is the mirror that, in the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki, was used to lure Amaterasu out of the cave of Amano-Izumi when she hid and the world fell into darkness. [S1][S2] Hung before the cave, its reflected light drew the goddess out, restoring the light of the world. It is one of the Three Sacred Treasures (the Regalia) and the emblem of the imperial line's descent from the sun-goddess. As a regalia it is the emblem of truth, purity, and the sovereign's divine right.
interesting_facts: Yata no Kagami is one of the Three Sacred Treasures (the Regalia) alongside the Kusanagi and the Yasakani no Magatama.
uncertainty_notes: The regalia are not publicly displayed or examined; the physical mirror's survival and form are a matter of tradition, not of public verification.

description_short: The jewel of sovereignty and longevity; one of the Three Sacred Treasures of Japan.
description_long: Yasakani no Magatama ('the Eight-Span Jewel') is the magatama — the comma-shaped jewel — that is one of the Three Sacred Treasures (the Regalia). In the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki it is the jewel of the imperial line, the emblem of the sovereign's divine right and of purity. [S1][S2] As a regalia it is the emblem of sovereignty, longevity, and the enduring right of the imperial line. In later tradition the magatama is a charm of longevity.
interesting_facts: Yasakani no Magatama is one of the Three Sacred Treasures (the Regalia) alongside the Kusanagi and the Yata no Kagami.
uncertainty_notes: The regalia are not publicly displayed or examined; the physical magatama's survival and form are a matter of tradition, not of public verification.

description_short: The celestial lance with which the islands of Japan were formed; the scepter of the creator-god.
description_long: Ame-no-Nuboko ('the Heavenly Lake-Lance') is the lance with which, in the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki, Izanagi and Izanami stood on the Bridge of Heaven and stirred the brine below, forming the islands of Japan. [S1][S2] It is the instrument of the creative act and the emblem of the power to make the world. It is the scepter of the creator-god, the emblem of the cosmic order that the islands embody.
interesting_facts: Ame-no-Nuboko is the Japanese equivalent of the "world-making" instrument; it is the scepter of the creator-god.
uncertainty_notes: The lance's later fate and its relationship to the other Regalia are not specified in the surviving sources.
